F1.details: Test was renamed from test_get_gpu_backtest_engine_class_returns_none_on_runtime_error to test_get_gpu_backtest_engine_class_returns_none_on_import_error (broader scope) and parametrized over all 4 exception types: ImportError, RuntimeError, OSError, AttributeError. The test now uses real exception instances including a realistic AttributeError message ('partially initialized module "jax" has no attribute "version"'). All 4 parametrized cases + 2 existing tests pass (6 total in tests/unit/test_jax_compat.py). This locks in the full catch contract: any future refactor that drops one of the four exception types from _GPU_ENGINE_ERRORS will be caught by the parametrized test. AC#2 is now actually verified by an automated test.

F2.details: Module docstring now reads: 'JAX can fail during import or initialisation with a variety of exceptions: ImportError, RuntimeError, OSError, or AttributeError (e.g. AVX/NumPy incompatibility, partially-initialised module state). All are caught so that callers fall back to CPUBacktestEngine.' The rationale now correctly mentions all 4 exception types, including the specific reason for AttributeError (partially-initialised module state) that was the trigger for this task. Future readers will understand why AttributeError is in the catch list.

correctness.notes: The try/except in get_gpu_backtest_engine_class() catches _GPU_ENGINE_ERRORS by reference, so adding AttributeError to the tuple is sufficient to satisfy AC#1 and AC#2. The diff is minimal: 1 line insertion in the tuple, 2 lines in docstring (3 added, 2 removed) in jax_compat.py; 1 test function rename with 4-way parametrization in test_jax_compat.py. No other logic changes.

security.notes: Defensive catch widening has no security implications. No new I/O, no new external calls, no new attack surface.

edge_cases.notes: The parametrized test now covers all four exception types in _GPU_ENGINE_ERRORS (ImportError, RuntimeError, OSError, AttributeError). Each case is exercised via the same monkeypatched __import__ path, so the catch contract is fully locked in. The slightly broader AttributeError net (vs. the original three exceptions) is acceptable: the CPU fallback is the correct behavior when JAX is unusable, and Phase 2/3 callers already treat None as 'use CPU'.

maintainability.notes: Test rename from 'on_runtime_error' to 'on_import_error' is more accurate since the test now exercises 4 exception types, not just RuntimeError. No stale references to the old test name exist elsewhere in the codebase (verified via grep). Docstring is now self-documenting: a new reader immediately sees why each exception type is in the catch list.

test_adequacy.notes: 6 tests pass under PYTEST_LOW_MEMORY=1. The parametrized test_get_gpu_backtest_engine_class_returns_none_on_import_error provides 4 cases (one per exception type) and serves as a strong regression guard. The two existing integration-style tests (test_cpu_engine_import_without_jax, test_run_pipeline_imports_on_cpu_only_host) continue to verify the package import chain works without jax installed.
